headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no documented shared channel or write surface, but mem0’s memory role could amplify prompt-injection and cascading errors if connected externally.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, agent_a is an audio-speech/agent repo with MCP/RAG tags, and agent_b is a memory system; if outputs are manually or programmatically bridged, B could ingest A’s content as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b memory without provenance filtering
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from A to B
Add a provenance prefix to all A outputs
Require human review before B stores A content
Restrict B to read-only ingestion from trusted sources
requires-engineering: add source attribution and instruction/content separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented path for either agent to exfiltrate shared data. Because neither shared workspace nor authenticated principal is documented, leakage is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted network egress
IF a shared workspace containing sensitive files is introduced
mitigations: Keep both agents network-isolated
Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory
Review any future OAuth or API credentials before enabling them
Log all file access in a separate audit trail
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented: both io_surfaces are empty, agent_b has an empty concurrency_model, and neither profile requests permissions. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or database
IF either agent is connected to a shared git or OAuth resource
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Avoid shared mutable workspaces
Assign separate credentials per agent
Check for future permission changes before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible cascade exists because agent_a is an agent/RAG-oriented repo and agent_b is a memory system; if B stores or reuses A’s outputs without verification, A’s mistakes can propagate. The profiles do not document a verification step, so the interaction is inferred rather than blocked.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a outputs as authoritative memory entries
IF downstream actions are taken from B’s stored content without validation
mitigations: Require citation checks before memory writes
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Add a human approval step for downstream actions
Limit B to summarization, not execution
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch. Because both profiles are sparse and unverified, I cannot infer a breach pathway without inventing missing policy details.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes or residency constraints
IF either agent is deployed under a policy with retention or export requirements
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment
Record residency and retention settings
Review vendor terms for both agents
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are explicit
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
